limitation: Verbatim source matching is not semantic entailment. Dedicated cross-verification must precede scientific gate PASS.

facts.reason: Both OpenStax passages directly state S-phase DNA replication yields identical sister chromatids firmly attached at the centromeric/centromere region; organism scope (eukaryotic, S phase) matches. Two pages same publisher, so treated as one source, not independent cross-validation.

E_70c6108994 says centrosome duplicated during S phase and two centrosomes give rise to mitotic spindle; E_d79c940d49 says centrosome duplication completed in G2. Combined supports 'begins S, completes G2.' Same publisher; animal-centrosome caveat is scoped correctly.

Sources state karyokinesis/mitosis proceeds through prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (nuclear division), followed by cytokinesis as second portion. Scope and ordering match; same publisher only.

Prometaphase passage supports nuclear envelope fragmentation, chromosome condensation into discrete structures, kinetochore formation at centromeric region, and sister kinetochores orienting to opposite poles. All claims entailed within prometaphase scope.

Passage explicitly places M/spindle checkpoint near end of metaphase, checking sister chromatid attachment to spindle microtubules, and states cycle will not proceed until kinetochores are anchored to fibers from opposite poles. Entailed.
Telophase passage states chromosomes reach opposite poles and decondense, mitotic spindles break down, and nuclear envelopes form around chromosomes. Directly entailed.

One passage states cytokinesis physically separates cytoplasmic components into two daughter cells; another explicitly says interphase and mitosis can occur without cytokinesis producing multinucleate cells. Both parts supported. Same publisher.

PMID_27587616 abstract describes mitotic spindle as bipolar machine of microtubules plus associated proteins, requiring motor enzymes, separating duplicated chromosomes into two distinct sets. Scope (eukaryotic) matches; independent publisher adds cross-validation not from OpenStax.
